text:
Maya: Drafting an operator/upgrade API proposal to coordinate private deployment upgrades when customers manage their own networking. Brainstorming phases and failure modes — pinging eng-runtime, eng-platform, and support for quick feedback.

Alex: Quick Q — is this additive to the installer/bundle flows or meant to replace the manual on-prem steps?

Maya: Additive. Idea is a small control-plane contract (CRD) our on-prem operator reconciles to orchestrate upgrades while leaving network control to customers. Phases: preflight, drain, staged apply, postflight, verify, rollback.

Kevin: CRD sketch looks sensible. Early thought: keep it declarative and minimal. Example sketch: 

```
kind: PrivateUpgrade
apiVersion: redwood.io/v1
metadata:
  name: upgrade-1745550000
spec:
  targetVersion: 4.2.0
  strategy: staged
  canaryPercent: 5
  maintenanceWindow: "2026-05-12T22:00:00Z"
  preflight:
    checks: [k8s_version, ip_quota, certs_valid, egress_probe]
  network:
    preserveEgressIP: true
    egressMode: customer-controlled
  rollbackOn:
    errorRatePct: 3
    p50LatencyIncreasePct: 30
```

Kevin: Operator flow: run preflight, annotate tenants/nodes, drain, apply, watch metrics, promote canary, continue or rollback. Metric hooks + manual abort.

Sasha: Support notes — we need clear run IDs surfaced to customers and a human-readable log (not just k8s events). Also customers will require an opt-out toggle and a visible maintenance window; some will block any automated rollouts.

deploy-bot: Upgrade orchestration job queued -> staging-upgrade-1745550000 (status: queued) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Alex: Networking question — many customers use NAT-relay or an egress-proxy to preserve outbound IPs. How do we validate egress after an upgrade? We need an explicit postflight egress probe and a fallback path if IPs change.

Maya: Agreed. Add `egress_probe` in preflight and postflight. Probe should check both control-plane reachability and outbound IP mapping for tenant traffic. If mapping changed unexpectedly, operator should pause and surface remediation steps.

Kevin: Also consider a compatibility-mode fallback: if new GPU driver or runtime mismatch detected, operator can switch that node to a quantized/compat runtime automatically (with explicit consent) to reduce downtime. Keep this opt-in.

Sasha: For customer comms — propose default notifications: email + webhook on start/success/failure, with run-id and short reason codes. Boilerplate for incident/contact points so support can escalate quickly.

Maya: Action items: Kevin -> produce proto/CRD + reconciliation pseudo-code by EOD Wednesday. Alex -> draft runbook for relay/egress probes + remediation steps. Sasha -> draft customer comms + opt-out language. I'll collate and put a PR up for the design doc. Reconvene Friday AM. Any objections?

Alex: +1

Kevin: Can do, aiming Thu morning if blocked by runtime tests.

Sasha: I'll have comms template in 24h.

Maya: Thanks team :tada:
